processed_notes.note_text:
Phone Re-Screening – Columbia (11/10/26)

I called Matthew Young to update his screening now that he’s moved to Columbia. He’s living at an Oxford House and is happy there. He has his birth certificate and state ID but not his Social Security card. His license is still suspended. 

He’s still taking Suboxone through Prisma Health Recovery, where he meets with a peer support specialist, a counselor, and a doctor and gets urine screens. His next appointment is Thursday. He schedules visits himself, so they won’t conflict with program hours. He shared that after returning to Columbia without housing, he ended up in a bad spot and used meth once. He’s been clean since 10/23/26. Five recovery meetings a week are mandatory for him, and he usually goes to 6–7. His Prisma Health participation along with living in an Oxford House looks covers the recovery program requirements for now. He'll be on the waitlist for at least a month most likely, so we can check back in on his sobriety before enrolling him.

Transportation: his e-bike arrives tomorrow, and the center is about 3 miles from him. He was hired for a maintenance position at McDonald’s and is waiting to be trained. The hours are about 5pm–1am, so they won’t conflict with the program. He hopes the program leads to a better job and says he’s skilled in remodeling. If the program doesn’t turn up something better, he’ll stay with what he has.

Next steps: he’s on the Columbia waitlist, which has about 13 people and is moving slowly. He wants updates rather than reentry navigation help. He has a meeting Monday (11/16) at 9am with Vocational Rehab to see what support they can offer.

I called Matthew Young back. He’s now living in the Columbia area at an Oxford House and wants to move forward with the program at the Columbia Center. He ordered an e-bike that should arrive in about a day. He lives close to the center, so he expects to be able to get there.

When he last spoke with Kat, he had two jobs, window installation and McDonald’s. He’s not working either one right now. The window installation company has very little work. McDonald’s is on hold because its late hours conflict with his 30-day blackout period at the Oxford House, which ends in about two weeks. McDonald’s will let him come back after that, but only on night shifts.

Because he’s moved and his situation has changed, I told him we’d need to redo his screening. I also warned him that the Columbia waitlist is long and could mean a wait of a month or more. He still wants to go ahead.

Updated that he is living in an Oxford house in Columbia and started two jobs: window instillation and a job at McDonalds and he is going to work both. No longer interested in RN, removing him from program.

Came by the center Friday and let Kat know that he was kicked out of Shield. He plans to take the bus back to Columbia where his family is. I reached out over text (had already left the office Friday) and told him we could reach out to our Columbia housing partners once he has an idea of his budget for rent. I removed him from the Charleston waitlist this morning and will not add him to the Columbia waitlist until he is stable in Columbia.

Came by the center to give me his phone number. May want to relocate to Columbia because he was put on Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) and isn't sure if Shield will allow that. He's from Columbia and his family is there. If he does need to relocate, he is interested in finding housing as well as transportation options to get there.

Currently at Shield Ministries. Has access to necessary prescriptions. Has birth certificate and state ID. NO social security card. NO phone. Used Heroin and Meth in the past, says he's been sober 1.5 years. No drug-related charges that I can find. Receiving a settlement next week that he plans to use to pay off his license reinstatement fees. Signed up for StaffZone for work as he waits for a spot to open up in Charleston. Looking for support in the process of getting his DL back. He has no phone, so I gave him my card to use the Shield phone and let him know he can walk in as well.
